title: Breast anatomy: lobules, ducts and supporting tissue
description: A modified sweat gland: glandular lobules make milk, ducts carry it, fat gives shape, and lymph drains mostly to the axilla — which is why breast cancer staging checks axillary nodes.

questions.question: What structures make up breast tissue?
questions.answer: Breast tissue includes glandular lobules, a branching duct network, connective-tissue support, fat, vessels and nerves. Ducts open at the nipple.

questions.question: Are breast lobules and milk ducts the same thing?
questions.answer: No. Lobules contain milk-producing units; ducts transport secretions toward the nipple. Both are embedded in supporting connective and fatty tissue.

questions.question: What are the lobules (glandular)?
questions.answer: Secretory alveolar clusters at duct ends. Function: Milk production under prolactin.

questions.question: Where is the lactiferous ducts located?
questions.answer: 15–20 branching channels to the nipple. Function: Transport milk.

questions.question: What is the function of the axillary lymph nodes?
questions.answer: Function: Immune surveillance of the breast. 75% of breast lymph drains here.
